characters.name: Concetta Ricci
characters.arc: Protagonist, 43, postal clerk — wants to understand why Andrea wrote if he never came back
characters.voice: precise, internal, avoids direct eye contact

characters.name: Active Arc
characters.arc: In Chapter 8, Concetta secretly visits the harbor master to ask about ship manifests, hiding her inquiry from Enzo, revealing her growing distrust of her current life.

characters.name: Enzo Marino
characters.arc: Husband, 45, widower fisherman — wants to keep the peace and protect his stepchildren

characters.name: Active Arc
characters.arc: In Chapter 10, Enzo catches Concetta reading the second letter and throws it into the sea without asking what it says, asserting his control through silence rather than violence.

characters.name: Padre Salvatore
characters.arc: Parish priest, 60 — wants to maintain the village’s narrative of heroic sacrifice

characters.name: Active Arc
characters.arc: In Chapter 9, Padre Salvatore confronts Concetta at the church door, warning her that digging up the past is an act of vanity, not piety, driving her toward isolation.

characters.name: Nonna Rosa
characters.arc: Mother-in-law, 72 — wants to preserve Andrea’s memory as perfect

characters.name: Active Arc
characters.arc: In Chapter 12, Nonna Rosa discovers the letters and burns one in front of Concetta, forcing Concetta to physically intervene and save the final piece of evidence.

characters.name: Luca
characters.arc: Andrea’s eldest son from his first marriage, 19 — wants to leave the village

characters.name: Active Arc
characters.arc: In Chapter 11, Luca helps Concetta decode a cipher in the third letter, motivated by his own desire to escape the village, aligning his rebellion with her quest.

settings.name: La Posta
settings.description: The village post office — smells of damp paper and stale tobacco; the air is thick with dust motes dancing in shafts of light.

settings.name: La Barca
settings.description: Enzo’s fishing boat, *La Speranza* — smells of brine, rust, and wet canvas; the wood groans under the tension of the tide.

settings.name: Casa Marino
settings.description: The family home in the village center — smells of dried oregano and simmering tomato sauce; the tiles are cool and hard beneath bare feet.

settings.name: Il Cimitero
settings.description: The cemetery on the hill overlooking the bay — smells of cypress resin and dry earth; the wind carries the distant sound of waves crashing against cliffs.

plot_points.description: Concetta sorts mail and finds the first letter addressed to "Andrea Marino, Deceased" — introduces the anomaly.
Concetta reads the letter; it mentions a Marseille address and a date from 1950 — raises the question of survival.
Flashback: Summer 1942, Andrea packing his bags, the tension of departure — establishes the love and the fear.
The second letter arrives; it contains a photograph of Andrea, older, in Palermo — forces Concetta to acknowledge he lived without her.
Concetta visits Padre Salvatore to ask about the death certificate; he dismisses her concerns — shifts conflict from mystery to institutional gaslighting.
Concetta asks the harbor master about ships; he refuses to speak — confirms the cover-up is widespread.
Enzo throws the second letter into the sea — raises the stakes of domestic conflict.
Nonna Rosa burns one letter; Concetta saves the final one, leading to a silent, devastating confrontation with Enzo — the point of no return.
Concetta decodes the final letter’s coordinates; she decides not to go, but to write back — resolves the internal conflict.
Concetta sends the letter to Palermo and burns her own journals — accepts the ambiguity of her life.

voice: Close third person, past tense, restrained and observant, focusing on the tactile weight of objects and the suffocating humidity of the Mediterranean summer.
